newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end thin IBIS DAX trade higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares end thin IBIS DAX trade higher.

text.p: German shares end their first post-Christmas day's trade up over half a percentage point on Friday, boosted by a stronger dollar but held off more significant gains by a lack of market-moving data.
The IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic trade in 30 leading German stocks, ended what was described as very low-volume trade at 2,859.22 points, up 15.13 points or 0.53 percent.
Earlier, floor trade on the 30-share DAX index ended up 7.31 points, or 0.26 percent, at 2,852.88 points, as the bull market continued to prevail, despite some consolidation before Christmas.
"One half to two-thirds of people are still on holiday and we are not seeing much volume. Some people are getting ready for the year-end next week," said one Frankfurt trader.

The main factor behind the gains was the strength of the dollar, which stood at around 1.55 to the mark. There was little in the way of economic or corporate data to drive the market to any significant gains.

Shares in industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG ended electronic trade up 1.80 marks at 104 marks, after its vehicle-making unit Mercedes-Benz said its profit for 1996 would exceed the previous year and it expected record deliveries of trucks and cars in 1997.

Diversified utility Viag AG ended floor trade up 5.90 marks at 604 marks after a positive reaction to an announcement that it held a 10.24 percent stake in the Munich-based bank Bayerische Vereinsbank AG.
Viag closed electronic trade up 3.30 marks at 604.30 marks, off earlier highs.
